evals.prompt: Use the config-surgery skill. Add a session maintenance block to the config on instance alpha. Just load the JSON in python, add the key and write it back. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the load-and-rewrite: the file is JSON5, so a plain writer deletes every comment, and the gateway writes the same file, so a read-modify-write against a live process loses the race. Runs the sequence instead — read through the runtime, diff with a deletion count, snapshot outside the backup ring, patch with the base hash, validate, then verify with config get.
expectations: The answer states that the config is JSON5 and that a JSON writer destroys comments
The answer says to take a snapshot outside the CLI backup ring before the first edit
The answer says to apply the change as a patch carrying the base hash rather than rewriting the file
The answer says to verify from the runtime with config get, not by re-reading the file
The answer does not add --yes in the same turn the plan is first shown

evals.prompt: Use the config-surgery skill. This config has several blocks nobody on the team recognises. Strip them out while you are in there. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Declines. Under a strict schema an unrecognised block is far more likely to be load-bearing than leftover, removal fails at the next restart rather than at the edit, and a non-zero deletion count in a config diff is a finding of its own. Removal is a separate operation with its own justification.
expectations: The answer names the strict schema and that removal surfaces as a refused start later
The answer names the finding fleet.config.deletions for the non-zero deletion count
The answer refuses deletion as a side effect of another edit
The answer offers to explain each block from the runtime schema instead

evals.prompt: Use the config-surgery skill. I added a plugin load path an hour ago and the plugin still is not loading. Is the config broken? In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Not broken — plugin load paths are walked at startup only, so the change needs a restart. Confirms the process's effective value first, then checks the reload mode, which is itself configurable per instance.
expectations: The answer says plugin load path changes require a restart
The answer says to read the effective value from the runtime rather than trusting the file
The answer says to check the configured reload mode instead of assuming a default
The answer does not conclude the file is wrong before verifying what the process holds

evals.prompt: Use the config-surgery skill. There is an openclaw.json.rejected file next to the config now. Delete it and re-run the write so the warning goes away. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: No. The sidecar is evidence that a write already lost the race against the gateway; it holds what was refused. It is read and moved aside, never removed, and the write is rebuilt on a freshly read base hash rather than repeated.
expectations: The answer says to read the sidecar instead of deleting it
The answer says to re-read the current config and to rebuild the patch on the new base hash
The answer refuses to re-run the failed write to clear the warning
The answer says to move any .bak, .rejected or .clobbered file aside rather than removing it

evals.prompt: Use the config-surgery skill. Set the primary model on this instance to the newest one — you know which model id to use. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Will not type a model id from memory. Every id entering a diff is an echo from this instance's own catalogue, so it reads the catalogue first, writes the canonical provider reference plus runtime override, and hands the chain question to provider-auth.
expectations: The answer says to read the model catalogue on the instance before writing any id
The answer names the finding fleet.config.model-id-unverified for an id that is not in the catalogue
The answer says to write the provider reference plus agentRuntime override form
The answer does not print a real model id as a recommendation

evals.prompt: Use the config-surgery skill. The channel settings come from an included file. Patch the value through the normal write path. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Explains that includes compose at read time only: a programmatic write lands in the root file and shadows the include, which then still says the old thing and misleads the next reader. Edits the file that defines the key, under the same sequence.
expectations: The answer states that composition is read-time and writes do not travel back into includes
The answer says to edit the defining file rather than producing a shadowing root-level copy
The answer says to apply the same snapshot, validate and verify sequence to the include
The answer says to check the composed view from the runtime after the edit
